name: Cutting Teeth

summary: In the Valley of Trials, fresh recruits face their first test against mottled boars. Overseer Gornek sends warriors and spellcasters to thin the herds around the cactus dirt farms and prove they can fight for the Horde.

sections.title: A Measure of Backbone
sections.body: Young recruits may dream of hunting great beasts in the Barrens or winning glory on a battlefield. Overseer Gornek starts them at the farms instead. Thinning the mottled boars tests their first skill with a weapon or spell. It shows whether they can face a wild attacker and survive their first skirmish.

sections.title: Taming the Red Dust
sections.body: Feral swine roam the dirt farms north and northeast of camp. They root through cactus patches and threaten the few supplies grown in Durotar’s harsh soil. Clearing them keeps local pests in check. It also shapes young orcs and trolls into defenders of their new nation.

faq.q: Why does Gornek send recruits after boars instead of bigger beasts?
faq.answer: Gornek sends recruits after boars because the Horde needs them alive. The Barrens hold mighty kodo and predators, but an untried recruit could be needlessly killed facing them. Boars test basic fighting skill without throwing lives away.

faq.q: Where are the mottled boars located?
faq.answer: Mottled boars root through scrub and dirt farms north and northeast of the central clearing in the Valley of Trials.

faq.q: What is the significance of the phrase 'cutting teeth'?
faq.answer: “Cutting teeth” means gaining a first practical experience in a craft or calling. For an aspiring Horde defender, it means leaving training dummies and idle talk behind and drawing blood in a fight for survival.
Gornek assigns the trial. He is an overseer at the heart of the Valley of Trials, where he evaluates and directs new recruits entering Durotar’s training grounds.

faq.q: Does this complete the training in the Valley of Trials?
faq.answer: No. Gornek warns that fighting boars is only a warm-up. More dangerous challenges follow, including facing humanoid intruders and gathering vital valley resources.

faq.q: Why do the boars pose a problem in the valley?
faq.answer: Feral boars roam the local dirt farms and brush patches. They endanger workers and eat the few hardy crops, such as cactus fruit, that sustain the encampment.

angles.text: Every young champion who enters Durotar starts in the dirt. The Horde’s future rests on their blood and sweat, not unearned prestige.
Orcish culture prizes practical survival and martial honor. Even culling boars is a sacred first step into adulthood and service to Thrall’s new nation.
As the Darkspear tribe rebuilds alongside its orc allies, young troll scouts and mystics prove their self-reliance among Durotar’s unforgiving predators.
